lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: The file header still claims 'All tests drive runGates with a fake spa…

nextStoryContext: US-R1-003 fixed the round-1 WARNING finding: test/check-all.test.ts's two full-manifest onResults tests ('onResults entries match manifest gate names in order' and the 14-name --json case) called runGates({ spawnFn: fn, onResults }) WITHOUT an explicit `gates` array, so runGates fell back to the real GATES manifest (scripts/check-all.ts). Since US-002 (CAM-488) that manifest includes two real in-process gates -- coverageGate and skipRatchetGate -- whose `run` fns call checkCoverage()/checkSkipRatchet() with their real (non-injected) getStagedDiff/readBudget/getSuiteOutput defaults: checkCoverage's default getStagedDiff shells a real `git diff --cached -U0 scripts/coverage-budget.json` (scripts/ratchet-diff.ts) and its default readBudget does a real readFileSync+JSON.parse of scripts/coverage-budget.json off disk. This silently gave two 'unit' tests an ambient git + cwd dependency, contradicting the file's own header claim ('no real subprocess is invoked') and the project's stated DI convention. Fix: added a `spawnOnlyGates()` helper in test/check-all.test.ts that maps the real GATES array to an all-spawn-shaped array (same name/order, cmd/args swapped to a fake 'bun <name>' pair per entry) -- derived from GATES rather than hand-duplicated, so it tracks the manifest automatically if gates are added/removed/reordered -- and passed it explicitly as `gates:` to both tests. Restated the file header (top of test/check-all.test.ts) to document this derivation and why it exists, rather than leaving the now-false 'no real subprocess is invoked' blanket claim. scripts/file-size-budget.json's test/check-all.test.ts ceiling raised 438->462 (actual gate-measured line count, content.split('\n').length) with a dated _ref note prepended and staged before the file-size gate was re-run, per the CAM-488 story rubric. Full spine verified green: bun run typecheck (0 errors), bun test (5953 pass / 0 fail), bun run check:all (exit 0, all 14 gates ok, including the now-isolated 'coverage' gate itself which legitimately still does real I/O when check:all runs for real -- only the two unit tests in check-all.test.ts were the DI violation). No more round-1 findings remain in prd.json as of this write; supervisor should proceed past round-1 review remediation.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Pure internal test-DI fix (bun:test only, already used identically elsewhere in this exact file: describe/expect/test imports unchanged, no new external library surface touched).
